examples.en: Did you wait long?

examples.en: Does it take long to get to the office? — No, it takes ten minutes.

My husband is always busy.
I always drink coffee in the morning.
This restaurant is always crowded.
The cafe in front of the office is always quiet.

dict_examples.en: He always reads the newspaper in the morning.

explain_en: 늘, 항상 and 언제나 are all similar. 늘 is the shortest. It usually goes right before the verb or adjective.

p.n: Almost the same; 항상 is slightly more neutral or formal.

examples.en: The new timetable is out. There's no class on Fridays.

explain_en: 시간표 is for fixed tables like classes, buses and trains. For personal plans, say 일정 or 스케줄.

en: this time (a time just named or shown)

examples.ko: 목요일 오전 열 시, 이때 어때요?

examples.en: Look here. There's a movie at seven on Friday. Shall we watch it then?

examples.ko: 수업은 열 시예요. 이때 학교에서 만나요.

examples.en: Shall I call at 4 p.m.? Are you free then?

It's finally raining! It's been so hot.

explain: 드디어는 오래 기다린 일이 마침내 될 때 써요. 좋은 일에 써요. 나쁜 일에는 ‘결국’을 써요.

examples.en: Thursdays are always fine for me.
That child is always smiling.
My younger sibling always drinks coffee.
The library is always quiet.
Come over to our place anytime.

explain: 언제나는 ‘always’와 ‘anytime’ 두 뜻이 있어요. ‘언제’(when)와 달라요. ‘언제 와요?’는 질문이에요.

p.n: Almost the same; 언제나 stresses 'at any time'.

My usual quitting time is six.

explain_en: 평소 means an ordinary, non-special time. It is often used as “평소에”. It is handy when comparing with a special day.

examples.en: Wow, we said it at the same time!
They both raised their hands at the same time.
Two buses are coming at the same time.
My friend and I called each other at the same time.

examples.ko: 동시에 두 가지를 해요? — 아니요, 하나씩 해요.
examples.en: Do you do two things at the same time? — No, I do one at a time.

explain: 보통 “동시에”라고 말해요. “같이”는 사람이 함께 하는 거고, “동시에”는 같은 때에 일어나는 거예요.

explain_en: You almost always say 동시에. 같이 means doing something together with someone; 동시에 means happening at the very same moment.

examples.en: The sun is really strong today.
In winter the days are short.

explain_en: 해 is the sun in the sky, and it also counts years: 한 해, 두 해. You can see it inside 올해(this year) and 새해 (new year).

dis.h: everyday native word; also means a year

p.n: 태양 sounds more formal or scientific; 해 is everyday and also means a year.

examples.en: The sun rises around six.
In summer the sun rises early.

examples.ko: 내일 해가 몇 시에 떠요? — 일곱 시쯤이에요.
examples.en: What time does the sun rise tomorrow? — Around seven.
The sun is rising over the sea. It's really beautiful.
The moon rises at night. There are lots of stars too.

explain: 해, 달, 별은 모두 “뜨다”를 써요. 반대는 “지다”예요. 해가 뜨고, 해가 져요.

explain_en: The sun, moon and stars all use 뜨다 to rise. The opposite is 지다: 해가 뜨고, 해가 져요.

dis.h: short everyday verb; sun rises or floats

p.n: 뜨다 is the plain statement; 떠오르다 stresses the gradual rising.
